reference_summary: The paper presents retrieval-augmented generation as a way to combine a pretrained sequence-to-sequence model with an explicit non-parametric memory. Its implementation pairs BART with a dense Wikipedia index accessed by a neural retriever. RAG-Sequence uses the same retrieved document throughout an output sequence, whereas RAG-Token can condition different tokens on different documents. Experiments cover open-domain question answering, language generation, and fact verification. The authors report state-of-the-art results on three open-domain QA tasks and more specific, diverse, and factual generation than a parametric-only baseline.
annotation_note: Questions and references were written from the source paper before inspecting generated answers. Relevant chunks were judged against fixed 1000-character/150-overlap chunking.

questions.question: Which parametric and non-parametric components form the RAG model?
questions.reference_answer: The parametric memory is a pretrained seq2seq transformer, and the non-parametric memory is a dense vector index of Wikipedia accessed by a pretrained neural retriever.

questions.question: What external knowledge source and retriever does the implementation use?
questions.reference_answer: It uses a dense vector index of Wikipedia and the Dense Passage Retriever, with BART as the generator.

questions.question: How do RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token differ?
questions.reference_answer: RAG-Sequence uses the same retrieved document to generate the complete sequence. RAG-Token can draw a different latent document for each target token.

questions.question: Which four open-domain QA datasets were evaluated?
questions.reference_answer: The paper evaluated Natural Questions, TriviaQA, WebQuestions, and CuratedTrec, reporting Exact Match scores.

questions.question: What generation qualities improved relative to the BART baseline?
questions.reference_answer: On MS-MARCO and Jeopardy question generation, the RAG models produced responses that were more factual, specific, and diverse than the BART baseline.

questions.question: What Exact Match score did RAG achieve on SQuAD?
questions.reference_answer: Not reported. SQuAD is not one of the open-domain QA datasets evaluated in this paper.
